central_unknown: Mercedes' form at COTA after their Malaysia aero regression remains the key uncertainty — Russell is projected P2 by ML but the team's upgrade path is unclear, and whether Ferrari or McLaren close the gap on the high-speed Austin layout will determine optimal constructor selection.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 25.1 exp pts (37.8 proj), ppm 1.81, MEDIUM risk. Predicted to qualify P3 and finish P1 — the highest projected scorer on the grid. Channels consistently rank Verstappen as the top captain choice, and ML agrees. His 90% CI runs to 51.0 on the upside. Seven Driver of the Day awards this season add bonus upside. Clear consensus pick.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: George Russell
captains.reason: ML projects 23.4 exp pts (29.3 proj), ppm 0.68, MEDIUM risk, predicted P4→P2. Second-highest expected points on the grid. However, channels express caution about Mercedes' aero regression from Malaysia and potential for a second engine penalty later in the season. If Russell avoids penalties and Mercedes sort their package, he has genuine P2 upside. Low ppm (0.68) reflects his high price but raw scoring ceiling is strong.

buy.name: Max Verstappen
buy.note: ML's top projected driver at 37.8 proj pts. Strong COTA record, highest ppm among premium drivers at 1.81. Must-have.

buy.name: Charles Leclerc
buy.note: ML projects 22.0 exp pts (26.3 proj), ppm 1.33, value 0.91 — best value score among top-4 drivers. Predicted P2→P3. Channels note Leclerc is 'on the trend up' and Ferrari's race pace has been strong.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: ML projects 9.9 exp pts, ppm 1.21. Solid budget enabler predicted P8→P8. Frees up budget for premium drivers and constructors.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Channels highlight him as a differential — strong recent form (17 pts in Malaysia). Budget-friendly pick if you need funds for premium constructors. Not in ML top 8 but channels rate his upside.

consider.name: Lewis Hamilton
consider.note: ML projects 16.8 exp pts (17.4 proj), ppm 1.09. Predicted P5→P5. Solid floor but channels and ML both rank him below Leclerc as the preferred Ferrari driver pick.

consider.name: Sergio Perez
consider.note: Channels flag as transfer target/trap — ultra-cheap differential at 3M. Only 27% ownership in top 500. Volatile: scored 8-13 recently but also had a -18 DNF. Use only if building a mega-team and need extreme budget savings.

consider.name: Fernando Alonso
consider.note: Channels note he performs well at low-speed corner tracks (24 pts Netherlands, 17 pts Malaysia) but COTA is not that type of circuit. Sub-1% ownership in top 500 — true differential but risky at Austin specifically.

avoid: Carlos Sainz — high price (~13M) relative to projected output, predicted very low by ML in recent analysis
Oscar Piastri — ML projects only 12.4 proj pts at 23.4M price (ppm 0.50), poor value relative to Leclerc or Verstappen
Lando Norris — ML projects 14.8 proj pts at 26.1M (ppm 0.29), worst points-per-million among premium drivers despite talent

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No sprint this weekend reduces total scoring potential. Save for a sprint weekend or a week with clearer pace advantages and price swing opportunities.

chips.name: 3x Captain
chips.reason: Verstappen is the clear captain but his 90% CI extends to -11.5 on the downside (DNF prob 0.17). Better deployed on a sprint weekend where captain scoring is amplified across more sessions.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Non-sprint weekend limits total scoring ceiling. Channels and recent analysis suggest limitless is best used on sprint weekends or when there's a clear top-heavy field advantage.

chips.name: 4A / Final Fix
chips.reason: If you need to restructure after recent weeks, a Final Fix could be useful to pivot into the Verstappen + Mercedes + Ferrari template without transfer penalties. Evaluate after qualifying.

watch_items: Mercedes aero package selection for Russell vs Antonelli — older Baku-spec vs Malaysia-spec could create a performance split
George Russell potential second engine penalty later in the season — may affect long-term planning if you bring him in now
McLaren's COTA form: ML projects Norris/Piastri significantly below their price points (ppm 0.29 and 0.50) — avoid unless practice shows improvement
Sergio Perez price volatility: at 3M floor, any decent weekend triggers a price rise, but DNF risk makes him a trap if timed poorly
Red Bull constructor (32.7M, 60.5 proj pts) vs Mercedes constructor (34.0M, 68.0 proj pts) — price gap of 1.3M but ~7.5 pt expected gap favors Mercedes
Kimi Antonelli predicted to qualify P1 but finish P4 by ML — if race pace disappoints, Mercedes constructor ceiling is capped
arc: The United States GP is a non-sprint race that serves as a reset point after the Singapore-Malaysia stretch. Mercedes remain the top constructor projection (60.8 exp pts) but their aero regression creates medium-term uncertainty. Verstappen looks dominant here and at the upcoming Mexico GP, making him a strong hold through the next block. Ferrari's value score (1.84) makes them the best constructor buy, and Leclerc's upward trend suggests he could be a multi-week core hold. Budget drivers like Lawson and Hadjar are critical enablers — whoever you choose here should be someone you can hold through Mexico to avoid transfer penalties. Save your big chips for the remaining sprint weekends, and use this race to establish a stable core of Verstappen + one Mercedes driver + Ferrari constructor that can carry through the Latin American swing.
